citation: Saeki K, Machida M, Kinoshita Y, Takasawa R, Tanuma S 2011, Biol Pharm Bull 34(1):146-149

rights.why: Free to read on J-STAGE is not a licence to redistribute. The article carries a bare copyright notice, has no PMCID and no open deposit, and the crops reproduce the author's printed characters — panels, a table and four sentences. This file is the recipe that regenerates them from a copy of the PDF the reader already holds; the images are not published with this repository.

needles.why: A locator identifier alone is a promise. The needle is the search string that resolves the locator to a span on the printed page, so the chain — needle to span, span inside crop, crop to digest — can be checked by a command rather than by eye. Each needle occurs exactly once on its page and is a fragment of the snippet of the locator it names.
needles.table_rows: Where a locator quotes a table row, the row is not contiguous in the text layer — the columns are separate runs — so the needle is the one cell value that is unique on the page.
needles.why_a_corrupt_layer_can_still_carry_a_ne: This article's text layer is SUSPECT and is refused as an evidence surface: it renders × as U+0002, ± as U+0003, and drops µ outright. The needles are nevertheless searched in that layer, deliberately. A needle is a coordinate, not a quotation — it only has to land on the right span — so every needle here is chosen from a stretch the corruption did not touch. The evidence is the crop.
needles.why_some_crops_adjudicate_nothing: Five crops carry an empty `adjudicates` list. They are figure surfaces — Fig. 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 — whose content is raster, so there is no text span for a needle to resolve to. They are still pinned by digest, and the manifest locators that name them declare `surface: figure`. An empty list is the honest encoding of 'this crop IS the evidence', not of a missing needle.
